title: Story of the Split-Mouthed Schoolmaster (Português)

full_text:
Beside Master Mansur sat another tutor, Master Faraj, who possessed a wide scar across his upper lip that gave him a permanent, crooked grin.
When the students inquired how he gained his mark, Master Faraj smiled wryly:

'Ah, my young scholars, my scar was earned by the incurable disease of poking my nose into another man's kettle!

Thirty years ago, I was not a teacher, but an inquisitive apprentice tailor who could never mind his own stitching. Whenever an argument broke out in the street, I would abandon my needle and thrust myself into the fray, giving unsolicited opinions.

One afternoon, a fiery blacksmith and an equally stubborn coppersmith stood in the lane arguing fiercely over who owned an iron horseshoe found in the dirt.
Instead of letting them resolve their minor squabble, I pushed between them, puffed up my chest, and cried:
"Halt! As an impartial observer of human law, I shall examine the horseshoe and deliver a binding verdict!"

I seized the horseshoe. But alas! The blacksmith had only moments before pulled it straight from the glowing charcoal forge to cool it, and it was still scorching red beneath its black soot crust!

The burning iron seared through my fingers! In agonizing pain, I threw the horseshoe backward over my head without looking.
The flying horseshoe struck the coppersmith's prized brass samovar, which fell and shattered the blacksmith's clay water jug!
Both craftsmen, enraged by my clumsy interference, turned upon me together. The blacksmith swung a leather bellows, and the brass nozzle caught me squarely across the mouth, splitting my lip!

As the apothecary stitched my lip, he said: "Let this stitch remind thee that he who enters a fight uninvited always receives the hardest blow."

From that painful day, I gave up interfering in strangers' affairs. I became a schoolmaster, teaching children to guard their tongues and keep their hands upon their own work, for quiet discretion is the best guard of peace.'
moral: Unchecked meddling in matters that do not concern one leads to pain; discretion preserves the tongue and the jaw. [PT]
